mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep drifting up from already-depressed levels, more commuting and downtown circulation will raise retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rising for at least two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary outings away from shopping districts and suppresses retail and recreation demand within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20 points week-on-week or remains above 15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 14 days than over the previous 14 days after PARKS crosses the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, people are spending more time near home and fewer trips are being converted into retail visits, which keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays positive and TRANSIT remains below -30 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy mobility improves first, it signals easier local access and looser movement constraints, which then spill over into modest retail recovery after about one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive after being negative or near zero for at least two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM crosses from nonpositive to positive levels.

mechanism_narrative: A continuing seasonal lift in PARKS combined with stable RESIDENTIAL time indicates weather-driven outdoor substitution, which pulls discretionary spending away from retail and recreation over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 4 weeks while PARKS remains above 15 and RESIDENTIAL stays near 10 or higher.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES stops declining and begins to recover, discretionary shopping follows with a lag because weekday trips and lunch-time purchases increase around employment centers.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks after being flat or lower
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains unchanged or declines over the next 14 days after WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays far below baseline while GROCERY_PHARM keeps edging up, routine essential trips are replacing discretionary trips, and retail and recreation will weaken over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35 while GROCERY_PHARM is at or above -3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -35 and GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above -3.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a narrowing gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals broader permission to travel and work on-site, which should lift retail and recreation within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points over two weeks while WORKPLACES also improves
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
